scenario: A NaN on the text plane renders `nan` ([LCST.4.5.6]). The NaN is `inf - inf`, an expression [LDET.3.6.2] lets produce one: `t.a / t.z` is +Inf for a zero Float divisor, and +Inf minus itself is NaN. It never reaches a slot ([LEXP.4.2]); it is interpolated into a `log` message, which renders Floats through the canonical text ([LDET.3.2.7]). PATH PINNED: `ds_fmt_float` in `runtime/src/libds/float_fmt.c`, which both runtimes call (Mercury through `ds.float_text.canonical`). Whatever the NaN's sign — x86_64 and aarch64 produce different default NaNs — the text is `nan`.
rules_ds:
schema T scope logical:
    entity_id: String key
    a: Float mutable
    z: Float mutable

rule r:
    T t
->
    let q = t.a / t.z - t.a / t.z
    log info "q={q}"
